content:
Today, Instapaper launched the 10th version of its iPhone and iPad applications, adding multiple improvements and completely redesigning its web platform. The details are as follows.

"The biggest iOS app update in over a decade"

Instapaper today (via MacMagazine) announced an update to its iOS app, while adding a brand new AI narration feature to its Android app and significantly revamping its website.

Instapaper 10 for iOS adds support for Liquid Glass and introduces four reading fonts:

Literata: a serif font designed by Google for Google Play Books. New York: a serif font designed by Apple for iOS. Open Sans: a sans-serif font commissioned by Google. Atkinson Hyperlegible: a sans-serif font developed by the Braille Institute.

This update also adds home screen widgets, which Instapaper says can display the article you are currently reading and your most recently saved items, and let you start reading with a single tap.

Instapaper says that for iPad users, this update improves multitasking, while both iPhone and iPad users will notice more reliable background syncing, faster article downloads, and a redesigned onboarding experience.

Instapaper says today's update is the biggest in over a decade, and also includes:

Folder counts: all folders will now show the number of articles or notes they contain. If you find folder counts make you more anxious, you can turn them off under "Settings > Behaviour > Folder Counts". Folder sorting: to sort your folders or tags, tap the "…" menu next to the folder title and choose your preferred sort order. Article list appearance: we've added a compact mode, new typography and styles, and easier ways to adjust the article list appearance. In the article list, tap "…" and then tap "Appearance" to adjust style, font, and image thumbnails.

Finally, Instapaper has completely revamped its web platform, adding features such as a three-column reader and keyboard shortcuts, and the Android app now also supports AI narration.
